questions.q: Identify the grammatical function of the suffix "एर" in the phrase "एर एप्य" from the first poem, and state its modern Hindi equivalent.
questions.a: The suffix "एर" functions as the genitive case marker (कारक चिह्न) equivalent to modern Hindi "का/के/की", indicating possession or relationship. A wrong answer (e.g., identifying it as dative "को" or locative "में") reveals the student cannot distinguish Braj Bhasha case endings from modern Hindi, indicating a gap in recognizing dialectal morphological variation.

questions.q: Explain why the poet uses "पन" instead of standard Braj "पर" or modern Hindi "पर/में" in "रमि एर" and "एपक एर मफक्य-इकफक्य", and what phonological process this represents.
questions.a: "पन" represents the Braj Bhasha locative postposition where the dental nasal 'न' assimilates to the preceding labial 'प' (from मूल रूप 'पर' > 'पन' through nasal assimilation), creating a metrically convenient heavy syllable. A wrong answer treating "पन" as a separate lexical item or modern Hindi "पन" (abstract noun suffix) reveals the student cannot apply historical phonology to textual analysis.

questions.q: In the second poem, analyze the verb form "हख[ " in "हख[ वकÅ¡" and "हख[ विSडज" — identify its grammatical category, person, number, and the syntactic construction it participates in.
questions.a: "हख[" is the second person plural imperative form of the verb "होना" (to be/become), used here as an auxiliary in a causative construction ("हख[ वकÅ¡" = "make it happen", "हख[ विSडज" = "make him do"), addressing the listener(s) with authoritative force. A wrong answer identifying it as indicative mood or singular person reveals inability to parse imperative morphology in causative syntax.

questions.q: Compare the compound formation in "बू'ओज" (first poem) and "िक'कपज" (second poem) — identify the समास type for each, provide the विग्रह, and explain how the semantic relationship differs between the two compounds.
questions.a: "बू'ओज" = बहुव्रीहि समास (बू'ओज = बू'ओज यस्य सः — जिसके बाज हैं) functioning as an epithet for the addressee; "िक'कपज" = तत्पुरुष समास (िक'कस्य पज — कुछ का पुत्र) denoting a specific relational identity. A wrong answer classifying both as तत्पुरुष or both as बहुव्रीहि reveals inability to distinguish semantic head-modifier relationships in compound typology.

questions.q: Evaluate the poetic effect of retaining archaic Braj forms ("उहन", "इकु", "इ<ह्य", "टहक") alongside relatively modern forms ("हमारे", "तुम्हें", "करो") in the same poem — does this linguistic layering enhance or undermine the poem's authenticity as a folk devotional text? Justify with two specific examples.
questions.a: The linguistic layering enhances authenticity by mirroring the actual speech continuum of 17th-century Braj region where archaic and innovative forms coexisted; e.g., "उहन" (archaic pronoun) preserves oral tradition flavor while "तुम्हें" (modernized) ensures comprehensibility, and "इकु" (अपभ्रंश < एकु) maintains metrical brevity against "एक" — this code-mixing reflects living language, not artificial archaism. A wrong answer claiming inconsistency reveals misunderstanding of diglossia in medieval poetic registers.

questions.q: Compose two original lines in Braj Bhasha style using at least three grammatical features analyzed above (case marker एर, postposition पन, imperative हख[, compound formation), addressing a deity with a request, and provide the modern Hindi translation with grammatical gloss.
questions.a: Example: "एर चरणन पन हख[ धरहु मोहे / इकु कृपा करहु दीन बंधु सोहे" — Modern Hindi: "आपके चरणों में मुझे रख लीजिए / एक कृपा कर दीजिए दीनबंधु शोभते हैं" — Gloss: एर (का), चरणन (चरणों में - पन assimilation), हख[ (हो जाओ/कर दो - imperative causative), इकु (एक - अपभ्रंश), दीन बंधु (तत्पुरुष समास). A poor answer using only modern Hindi forms or incorrect case markings reveals inability to productively apply analyzed grammatical knowledge.
